scope: Newer/cohort/regional content review. No graph edits, relationship proposals accepted, promotions, publication, OpenAlex or exhaustive author-variant resolution.

sample.cohort_note: Recomputed contrasts explicitly use Canada/US 2015–2026 versus 2000–2009. Historical reports label their contrasts 2015–25 and 2020–25; retain these labels when quoting them, distinct from the public 2020–2026 series. The recomputed Canada/US recent denominator 1,893 matches the older labelled denominator. The historical Europe contrast is 2015–25 versus 2000–14, with denominators 1,351 versus 674.
composition_limits: Sampled strict History-programme PhDs, not all History PhDs or adjacent disciplines.
University, country, language and subfield mix changes over time; partly embargoed recent cohorts and US thinness before 2010 affect apparent growth.
Country describes dissertation programme/repository geography, not the geography studied.
Counts establish cited-work presence, not influence, agreement, field membership or rhetorical citation role.
Post-2000 works could not be cited by earlier cohorts; publication age and exposure must be considered.
A work-level count is a deduplicated dissertation union for that exact key. No edition, translation or author-key totals have been summed.

work_keys: W:rosenwein|emotional communities in the early middle ages

existing_coverage.detail: Febvre 1941 and Henri Wallon as a named resource; emotions have earlier roots here.
Description includes emotions; this is not detailed 2000 sframework coverage.
Reddy is covered through 1984/1987 labour/class work, not Navigation 2001.

proposals.missing_or_underdeveloped_content: No history-of-emotions entry/strand, no Rosenwein or Sara Ahmed indexed identity; Reddy emotives/emotional regimes and Rosenwein emotional communities are absent as methods.
proposals.proposed_action: Research a bounded emotions field or method entry with earlier roots and distinct 2001/2002/2006 frameworks; examine Ahmed as a related but nonidentical affect/political resource.
limits: Small corpus signal: recentCanada/USReddy 26/1893, Rosenwein article 22/1893; not a field-size ranking.
Publication after 2000 makes early zero baselines partly inevitable.
Do not equate emotions history with psychohistory or infer an influence chain from co-citation.

proposals.title: Social production of space inside existing spatial history

existing_coverage.detail: Existing field already covers cartography, Massey, McKittrick/Wynter and GIS; no wholesale spatial-turn absence.
Harvey is an existing indexed resource for space, capital and the cultural city.

proposals.missing_or_underdeveloped_content: Henri Lefebvre has no indexed identity or graph text; the production of space is a prominent framework work absent from this otherwise substantial field.
proposals.proposed_action: Add a researched Lefebvre identity and a social-production/representation/lived-space strand; connect to existing urban/spatial distinctions only where passages establish use.
limits: English 99 dated andFrench 26 dated are distinct work keys; never sum without dissertation union.
English 1991 translation,1992 paperback andFrench 1974 original must remain separate.
Corpus author key is Lefebvre surname; identify work, not every Lefebvre record.

proposals.title: Empire as layered jurisdiction and legal pluralism

existing_coverage.detail: Connected and comparative empire already covered, but these named works and authors are absent.
Colonial critique exists; not interchangeable with historical jurisdictional analysis.
Local legal records and diplomacy are present; no Benton/Stern/Burbank framework.

proposals.missing_or_underdeveloped_content: No Lauren Benton, Jane Burbank or Philip J.Stern identity and no named jurisdiction/sovereignty strand; territorial empire is not the only useful unit.
proposals.proposed_action: Research an imperial/legal-history strand covering jurisdictional multiplicity, corridors/enclaves and corporate sovereignty; first attach to global/post/political rather than presume a new school.
limits: Benton 75 dated includes 54/1893 recentCanada/US; search 2010 did not exist in 2000 sbaseline.
Stern surname has multiple scholars in corpus; use Company-State key and Philip J.Stern credit only.
Burbank/Cooper are joint authors; first-author work key must not erase Cooper.
Stratified z for Benton work is 1.299 versus unstratified 2.764: a content lead, not robust proof of general growth.

proposals.title: Cold War, interventions and decolonizing societies

existing_coverage.detail: Tuchman/Wedgwood/W.A.Williams do not cover this post 2000 global Cold War intervention.
Canadian political/international tradition is present but not equivalent to this global methodological debate.
World/global/connected history exists, mostly earlier synthesis, early-modern connections and divergence.

proposals.missing_or_underdeveloped_content: Westad has no indexed identity or graph text despite 79 dated dissertations; a twentieth-century international-history transformation remains invisible.
proposals.proposed_action: Research global Cold War as a political/global strand: superpower projects, Third World revolutions, intervention, development and local agency; compare older diplomatic interpretations using actual arguments.
limits: Canada/US 47/1893 recent vs 3/630 baseline, but 2005 publication and expandingUS sample affect contrast.
44/79 dated areUS and 28 CA; not a globally representative disciplinary census.
Stratified z 1.019 is modest; no claim of universal turn or established genealogy.

proposals.title: International institutions and anticolonial worldmaking

existing_coverage.detail: Anti-colonial history and new DuBois entry are covered; worldmaking is not simply a missing activist biography.
Connected histories already present, but League/UN institutional analysis and these work arguments are absent.
Pedersen is indexed for coediting Elkins/Pedersen 2005, not her 2015 mandates history.
Getachew is named as 2022 symposium reader, not indexed for Worldmaking 2019.

proposals.missing_or_underdeveloped_content: No sustained treatment of mandates, racialized international hierarchy and competing meanings of self-determination across nation-building and international projects.
proposals.proposed_action: Develop a carefully differentiated twentieth-century empire/internationalism strand or debate joining institutional history to anti-colonial political thought; retain Manela, Pedersen and Getachew differences.
limits: Getachew 19 dated comes entirely after 2019: shorter publication exposure cannot establish weak importance.
Pedersen 24 dated and Getachew 19 are small samples; below 20 public work cutoff is an export choice, not absence from corpus.
Manela key 50 dated vs 52 all strict; preserve this distinction.
No direct debate edges or influence claims without reading replies/citations.

proposals.title: Human-rights periodization beyond existing Hunt reception

existing_coverage.detail: Inventing Human Rights 2007 and Moyn/Bell 2007 criticism already covered; scope explicitly says no human-rights entry.
Moyn exists as critic via 2007 review, not Last Utopia 2010.
Hunt 2007 is already a cultural-history resource.

proposals.missing_or_underdeveloped_content: Last Utopia 2010 and its 1970 sbreakthrough argument are absent; existing 2007 critical reception should not be mistaken for a full later periodization debate.
proposals.proposed_action: Expand the rights debate from its Hunt 2007 anchor to include distinct origins/rupture questions, anticolonialism, international activism and the 1970 s; first read the principal works and direct critical exchanges.
limits: Moyn 44 dated vsHunt 31 are distinct books, not votes on their arguments.
Citations do not establish dissertations sided with either work.
Do not remove existing 2007 qualifications or promote Moyn as a field founder.

proposals.title: Postwar US political history: suburbs, race and conservatism

existing_coverage.detail: Sugrue is present for race and industrial change; urban history is not absent.
The new political history strand concerns Britain, not thisUS literature.
Progressive/consensus historiography is a different historical argument.

proposals.missing_or_underdeveloped_content: McGirr and Lassiter lack indexed identities or graph text; grassroots New Right and suburban colour-blind politics have no substantive strand.
proposals.proposed_action: Research aUSpostwar political/urban strand comparing grassroots conservatism, metropolitan privilege and racialized political economy; retain differences between party, movement and suburban histories.
limits: McGirr 75 of 90 datedciters andLassiter 77 of 81 areUS: strong regional, weak global generalization.
McGirr recentCanada/US 46/1893 vs 13/630 is only modest share change; selection should be about content rather than maximumgrowth.
McGirr original/2002 listing/2015 new-preface dates require edition checking.

proposals.title: Deindustrialization, class and neoliberal transformation

existing_coverage.detail: Labour history and class debates exist, but Cowie is absent.
Steven High’s Industrial Sunset (2003) already covers cross-border plant closures, 1969–84.
Sugrue already covers race and industrial change in postwar Detroit.
Capitalism entry concentrates on slavery, divergence, industrialization and corporate finance; no named Harvey/Cowie framework.
Harvey exists for space/capital and cultural city, not his 2005 neoliberalism history.
Heathrow/neoliberal Britain 2021 is already in chronology: neoliberalism is not wholly unmentioned.

proposals.missing_or_underdeveloped_content: Existing Canadian and US deindustrialization strands cover High and Sugrue. The specific missing content is a worked comparison between Cowie’s cultural-political class history and Harvey’s account of neoliberal restructuring.
proposals.proposed_action: Add a bounded labour/capitalism/political strand comparing Cowie cultural-political class history with Harvey political economy; future work should investigate distinct national chronologies and direct critics.
limits: Cowie 42 of 48 datedareUS; Harvey 36 of 56 US and 15 CA.
Cowie 40/1893 recent versus 0 baseline partly reflects 2010 publication.
Harvey 2005 is a framework use candidate, but citation alone cannot identify function.
Do not conflate deindustrialization, conservatism and neoliberalism as one automatic process.

proposals.title: Regimes of historicity and presentism

existing_coverage.detail: Historical time is already covered through Koselleck.
New standalone entry preserves conceptual history/time; Hartog is absent.
Memory/heritage inquiry exists; no Hartog bridge.
Presentism 2002 source is present, but this does not supply Hartog 2003 concept.

proposals.missing_or_underdeveloped_content: Hartog is not indexed; regimes of historicity as a heuristic and the debated diagnosis of presentism are absent.
proposals.proposed_action: Research a temporal-experience strand linking conceptual history, memory and historical knowledge; distinguish analytical tool from universal era diagnosis.
limits: 42 of 59 dated citers are FR and 17 CA: a French-language and regional signal.
The historical Europe contrast is 35/1,351 recent versus 7/674 baseline, labelled 2015–25 versus 2000–14; these are not Canada/US denominators.
French 2003, revised French editions and English 2015 must not be conflated.
Existing Koselleck coverage does not prove an influence edge; the publisher names him as an inspiration.

existing_coverage.detail: Public use of past is present but is not a substitute for research on historical learning and disciplinary thinking.
Elton/Skinnertraining is present; not the same as history-didactics research.
Collective memory is present; historical consciousness and classroom source reasoning need differentiation.

proposals.missing_or_underdeveloped_content: No indexed Rüsen, Wineburg or Seixas and no history-education field/strand despite a coherent Swedish-didactics corpus niche.
proposals.proposed_action: Review scope before creating a field; an initial publichistory/philhistorystrand can explain historical orientation, narrative competence and historical source reasoning, with proper joint-credit for Big Six.
limits: Swedish citers: Wineburg 12/20, Rüsen History 14/18, Swedish collection 22/22, Big Six 7/11. This reflects Swedish History-programme composition, not universal History PhD reading.
Rüsen English 2005 and Swedish 2004 are distinct works; do not sum as editions without checking contents.
Wineburg book 2001 is distinct from the same-title article 1998 and reprint 2010.
Big Six is jointly credited to Peter Seixas and Tom Morton. The project bibliography lists 2012 while the frozen corpus gives 2013; check the cited edition before chronology work.
